findings.text: Export a zero-reporting guest read under vgic_mmio_read_raz and an all-ones reporting guest read under vgic_mmio_read_rao, plus a discarding guest write under vgic_mmio_write_wi and a discarding userspace write reporting success under vgic_mmio_uaccess_write_wi.

Export guest and userspace state readers that present per-interrupt windows as compact bit or byte aggregates: group membership under vgic_mmio_read_group, enable state under vgic_mmio_read_enable, pending state under vgic_mmio_read_pending with userspace form under vgic_uaccess_read_pending, activity under vgic_mmio_read_active with userspace form under vgic_uaccess_read_active, priority bytes under vgic_mmio_read_priority, and trigger configuration under vgic_mmio_read_config.

Export enable modifiers that act only on interrupts whose bit is set in the write value: guest set under vgic_mmio_write_senable and guest clear under vgic_mmio_write_cenable, plus userspace set under vgic_uaccess_write_senable and userspace clear under vgic_uaccess_write_cenable, where userspace forms report success and guest forms report no value.

Export pending and active modifiers as thin entry wrappers: guest pending set under vgic_mmio_write_spending and guest pending clear under vgic_mmio_write_cpending delegate to shared internal pending handling with guest context, while active set uses guest form under vgic_mmio_write_sactive with userspace form under vgic_mmio_uaccess_write_sactive and active clear offers userspace form under vgic_mmio_uaccess_write_cactive around shared internal active handling.

Export the MMIO dispatch contract under dispatch_mmio_read with companion dispatch_mmio_write published through kvm_io_gic_ops, supported by a region ordering comparator under match_region, bus to host and host to bus endian adapters under vgic_data_mmio_bus_to_host plus vgic_data_host_to_mmio_bus, and a container accessor under kvm_to_vgic_iodev that recovers the virtual GIC device from the generic I/O device.

Interrupt windows are derived from the faulting address with a density that depends on register class: single-bit-per-interrupt encodings for group plus enable plus pending plus active cover eight interrupts per accessed byte, priority covers one interrupt per byte, and configuration covers four interrupts per byte.

The version-three redistributor emulation exposes a sixty-four KiB biased window where group, enable-set, enable-clear, pending-set, pending-clear, active-set, active-clear, priority, configuration, modulation and access-control registers each occupy fixed offsets with fixed spans and handler assignments; single-bit words span four bytes, priority spans thirty-two bytes with byte and word access, configuration spans eight bytes with word access, and modulation plus access-control words read as zero and ignore writes.

Priority writes retain only the implemented high-order bits of each priority byte and notify virtual SGI state when the target is a hardware-backed software-generated interrupt; configuration reads report edge-triggered interrupts with a fixed two-bit pattern and level otherwise, while configuration writes ignore private interrupts below the private count known as VGIC_NR_PRIVATE_IRQS and select between VGIC_CONFIG_EDGE with companion VGIC_CONFIG_LEVEL from the odd bit of each two-bit field for shared interrupts, with priority width governed by VGIC_PRI_BITS.

Guest views of activity are serialized by a configuration mutex held across a prepare and finish pair surrounding the underlying virtual-state access, whereas userspace views bypass that mutex and prepare-finish pair and observe or replace the same virtual state directly; both paths report only virtual activity even for hardware-backed interrupts.

The hypervisor trap mask for the virtual CPU interface is composed from four boot-configurable requests covering group zero plus group one plus common plus direct-invalid handling, further forced by errata and capability probes so that Cavium and broken-SEIS hardware force group traps with broken-SEIS also forcing direct-invalid trapping, and absence of hardware direct-invalid support forces common trapping, materialized through ICH_HCR_EL2_TALL0 with companion ICH_HCR_EL2_TALL1 and companion ICH_HCR_EL2_TC and companion ICH_HCR_EL2_TDIR.

Virtualization trap register patching probes the interface version through a direct system-register read when running in hypervisor mode and through a hypercall otherwise, leaves patched code untouched when hypervisor mode is unavailable or when neither legacy nor version-three CPU-interface support nor broken-SEIS handling is present or when the hypercall reports a stub error, clears the SEIS indication on broken hardware, and otherwise materializes the probed value into the patched instruction sequence.

Dispatch treats a missing region as architectural no-op with zero-filled reads and ignored writes, routes CPU-interface and distributor accesses with the faulting CPU context while redistributor accesses use the bound redistributor CPU and ITS accesses use VM plus ITS context, orders region lookup by offset containment, and converts one-byte values unchanged with two, four and default-width values passed through little-endian helpers in opposite directions on read versus write paths.

Mutations of enable plus priority plus configuration state and pending sampling are serialized by a per-interrupt raw spinlock acquired with interrupt state saved and restored across the critical section, with the guest enable-set path transferring ownership of the held lock to a queue helper on queuing paths; group plus enable plus internal-active sampling reads observe without acquiring that lock.

Guest active reads and guest active set operations hold the virtual-machine configuration mutex across the whole prepare-access-finish span, while userspace active reads and writes and internal active helpers never acquire that mutex.

The register-region descriptor describes one MMIO window with a numeric base offset under reg_offset plus a byte span under len plus a per-interrupt width under bits_per_irq plus an access mask under access_flags, together with a guest read callable under read with an ITS-read alternate under its_read and a guest write callable under write with an ITS-write alternate under its_write, plus a userspace read callable under uaccess_read and a userspace write callable under uaccess_write with an ITS alternate under uaccess_its_write.

Nested state pairs a snapshot holding a first status word under eisr with a second under elrsr plus a pending indication under pend, alongside a per-CPU shadow holding a CPU-interface image under cpuif with a register-use mask under lr_map; module scope adds boolean trap controls and an enable flag plus static keys for trap and compatibility gating.

Pending observation selects its source by context: hardware-backed software-generated interrupts consult host irqchip state, guest views of mapped level interrupts consult the physical line level, userspace views under a version-three model consult a latched pending flag, and all other cases consult the generic virtual pending predicate, with host-query failures coerced to not-pending.

Enabling transitions carry side effects beyond the virtual flag: mapped level interrupts resample the physical line and release physical activity on a high-to-low edge observed while virtual activity is clear, hardware-backed software-generated interrupts enable the host interrupt only on a false-to-true edge and disabling clears the virtual flag while requesting asynchronous host disable when previously enabled, whereas userspace enable paths only flip the virtual flag and queue.

Entry occurs through generic I/O-device operations for MMIO reads and writes, through early boot-parameter parsers for trap and enable controls, and through alternative-patching handlers that compute the trap mask and materialize the probed version register at boot.

A host irqchip pending query that reports an error triggers a rate-limited warning identifying the host interrupt while the guest-visible pending bit is forced clear, so repeated host failures remain observable without stalling the MMIO path.
VGIC_ACCESS_8bit equals 1 and VGIC_ACCESS_32bit equals 2 and VGIC_ACCESS_64bit equals 4, used as combinable access-width masks.

Bit-density descriptors size their span as width times one thousand twenty-four divided by eight, full-range single-bit windows therefore span one hundred twenty-eight bytes, and the address mask helper computes width times one thousand twenty-four divided by eight minus one; length-based descriptors carry explicit spans with zero width, including four-byte single-bit words plus thirty-two-byte priority plus eight-byte configuration in the redistributor window.
The initial pending-table base value combines inner write-back cacheability with outer same-as-inner cacheability and inner shareability.
